_policy: Never hardcode prices in application code. This file is the only source.
A null price MUST render as '— price not verified' in the UI and MUST NOT
participate in any total. No fallbacks, no guesses.
Every model needs source_url + retrieved_at. CI fails when any
input_tiers / output_tiers express length-dependent pricing (Gemini Pro).
Each entry is {max_input_tokens, price}; the LAST entry must have
max_input_tokens: null meaning 'above all other tiers'. The cost engine
selects the tier from the actual input token count. Where tiers are
present, input_per_mtok / output_per_mtok hold the FIRST tier's price so
that display code with no tier awareness is still showing a real number.
cache_read_multiplier / cache_write_multiplier are relative to base input
price. cache_write_multiplier of 1.0 means the provider charges no write
premium (OpenAI's automatic caching); null means unverified.
batch_discount is a fraction: 0.5 means batch costs 50% of standard.

_deliberately_excluded.gemini-3.8-flash: Pricing is time-dependent ($0.75/$3.75 through 2026-12-31, then $1.50/$7.50). The schema has no valid-until field, so rather than ship a price that silently becomes wrong on 2027-01-01, this model is omitted. Add it with a valid_until field if it is needed.
_deliberately_excluded.gpt-5.5-pro / gpt-5.4-pro: No cached-input price listed and very high rates; omitted until needed.
_deliberately_excluded.batch_discounts_openai_google: Neither page consulted stated a per-model batch discount as a verifiable figure. The Gemini page says batch is 'typically 50%' of standard, which is not specific enough to compute with, so batch_discount is null for every OpenAI and Google model. The cost engine ignores the batch fraction and warns when a discount is unverified.
